validity.recommendation: no change to existence/classification; see separate attribution and spec concerns below for Owner split, Location scope, and ProposalMonth
validity.researcher_notes: AIM is real and correctly classified. Primary evidence: FERC Order Issuing Certificate and Approving Abandonment, Docket No. CP14-96-000, 150 FERC P 61,163 (issued March 3, 2015) -- the certificate authorizing Algonquin Gas Transmission, LLC to construct the 'Algonquin Incremental Market Project (AIM Project)' in NY/CT/RI/MA (live via Wayback capture of the original ferc.gov CalendarFiles URL, which now 404s directly on ferc.gov -- the live site has reorganized its document paths). Independently corroborated by WAMC (public radio, live): 'FERC Authorizes Algonquin To Put Most Of Its Pipeline Into Service' (Nov 1, 2016), which names the AIM Project, confirms it runs Rockland->Westchester->Putnam Counties NY into CT/RI/MA, states 342,000 Dth/d total capacity and the 26-in->42-in diameter replacement. Status=operating is further corroborated by Utility Dive (Jan 2019, live via Wayback) reporting an Algonquin pipeline outage affecting Rhode Island customers, and by the Wikipedia stub noting continued operation (gas releases/permit issues) through 2021-2022. Classification as FERC-jurisdictional interstate gas transmission (NGA section 7(c) certificate) is correct; PipelineType=transmission confirmed. No duplicate: AIM (P0150) is the discrete FERC CP14-96 certificate project, distinct from the Main Line (P0149, 1131 mi, Base Business) -- Enbridge's own Energy Infrastructure Assets factsheet explicitly separates 'Algonquin Base Business' from the 'Algonquin Incremental Market project' as distinct membership-interest classes, confirming these are correctly kept as separate GEM rows, not a duplicate/relabel. Opened and read to exhaustion: the FERC order (65+ pages), WAMC article, Wikipedia stub, Enbridge factsheet (page 69-70 of 156), Utility Dive article. Could not access/render: PHMSA primis.phmsa.dot.gov operator report (site has been rebuilt as a JS app; the static opid_288.html report path no longer serves plain content -- treated as inaccessible, not a deletion). Opened 6 of the ~35 distinct URLs in this row's harvested citation pool (several others were duplicates of the 18 bit.ly links that all resolve to en.wikipedia.org per the batch's measured conditions, and several protest-coverage/advocacy links -- moveon.org, sape2016.org, ecowatch.com, beyondextremeenergy.org -- are about opposition to the broader Algonquin corridor and were skimmed but yield no data-point corrections).

validity.recommendation: split Owner: keep Owner1=Enbridge but correct Owner1% to 85.00%, add Owner2=Eversource Energy at Owner2%=15.00% (AIM-project-specific, NOT the same split as the P0149 Main Line/Base Business, which is 100% Enbridge)
validity.researcher_notes: GEM currently records Owner1=Enbridge at 100.00% for this row. Enbridge's own 'Energy Infrastructure Assets' factsheet (live PDF, page 69-70 of 156) states verbatim: 'Ownership: Enbridge (100% Algonquin Base Business membership interest and 85% Algonquin Incremental Market project membership interest); Eversource Energy (15% Algonquin Incremental Market project membership interest)... Operator: Enbridge.' This factsheet explicitly distinguishes two separate ownership classes on the Algonquin system: the pre-existing 'Base Business' (100% Enbridge -- this is the correct split for the Main Line, P0149) and the 'Algonquin Incremental Market project' specifically (85% Enbridge / 15% Eversource Energy -- this row, P0150). The 100.00% Enbridge value currently on P0150 appears to be the Base Business split incorrectly copied onto the AIM row. This is a single-source (self-disclosure) finding at this point: I searched WAMC, the Wikipedia stub, the FERC CP14-96 order (which as sole-applicant certificate holder never mentions Eversource -- the equity stake looks like a separate corporate/financing arrangement outside the NGA certificate record, not evidence against it), and Utility Dive for a second, independent confirmation of the exact 85/15 split and found none within budget; a second source (an Eversource Energy SEC filing/investor disclosure naming its AIM equity stake) is owed. Operator is unaffected by this -- both classes share the same operator (Enbridge).

validity.recommendation: revisit EndState/Province (and consider EndLocation) -- the AIM Project's actual footprint and delivery points extend well beyond Westchester County, NY
validity.researcher_notes: GEM records this segment as Rockland County, NY -> Westchester County, NY (both StartState/Province and EndState/Province = New York). The FERC CP14-96 order (para 1, 4) states the AIM Project provides firm transportation 'from its existing recipient points in Ramapo, New York, to various city gate delivery points in Connecticut, Rhode Island, and Massachusetts,' and that the approximately 37.4 miles of new/replacement pipe is split across New York (Putnam, Rockland, Westchester Counties), Connecticut (Fairfield, Middlesex, Hartford, New London Counties), and Massachusetts (Norfolk, Suffolk Counties -- West Roxbury Lateral). WAMC corroborates: the project 'starts in Rockland County and moves through Westchester and Putnam Counties before heading into Connecticut, Rhode Island, and Massachusetts.' So while Rockland County (start) and Westchester County (a waypoint, not necessarily the true end) are both real and correctly named, labeling the segment's END as Westchester County, NY understates the project: the AIM Project's actual downstream termini are city-gate delivery points in CT, RI, and MA, and a material share of the new/replacement pipe mileage (17.3 of 37.4 mi) is physically in CT and MA, not NY. I'm not proposing a single replacement value because the project genuinely has multiple end states (CT/RI/MA), which the current single EndState/Province field can't cleanly capture -- flagging for a research/schema decision rather than guessing one state. This also means the LengthKnown=37.0 mi and Diameter=42 values are PROJECT-TOTAL figures (matching the FERC order's 'approximately 37.4 miles' and the NY/CT 42-inch replacement respectively), not a length confined to the labeled Rockland->Westchester, NY corridor alone -- worth flagging so a reviewer doesn't assume 37 mi lies entirely within the two named NY counties.

validity.recommendation: correct ProposalMonth from 8 (August) to 2 (February) -- Algonquin filed the AIM Project application on February 28, 2014, not in August
validity.researcher_notes: GEM records ProposalYear=2014, ProposalMonth=8. The FERC order states unambiguously, twice (para 1 and para 53): 'On February 28, 2014, Algonquin Gas Transmission, LLC (Algonquin) filed an application in Docket No. CP14-96-000 ... for authorization to construct and operate its Algonquin Incremental Market Project (AIM Project).' The year (2014) is right but the month is off by six months. I can't rule out August referring to some other August 2014 filing/notice in this docket (e.g., an August 6, 2014 draft EIS or an August 28, 2014 data request), but none of those are the 'proposal' (initial application) event, so I'm flagging it as likely wrong rather than confirmed-correct. This is a single primary source (the certificate order itself, which is the authoritative record of its own filing date) -- I did not find a second source stating the filing month explicitly (WAMC and Wikipedia don't give a filing date), but the FERC order's own docket history is about as authoritative as a date claim can get.

cross_row_leads.facts: Discussing cumulative impacts (para 117-118), the AIM order describes the then-contemplated Atlantic Bridge Project (P0154) as: 'may include 52.5 miles of new loop and replacement of existing pipeline and additional compression at six existing Algonquin compressor stations and one new compressor station... all 52.5 miles would be within or adjacent to existing rights-of-way.' It also states the Atlantic Bridge Project's 'earliest projected in-service date' at that time (the AIM order, issued March 2015) was November 2017. NOTE: this is preliminary/contemplated scope from a 2015 planning-stage discussion, before Atlantic Bridge's own FERC application/certificate -- treat as an early-estimate lead, not the final approved scope, and verify against Atlantic Bridge's own docket (CP16-9) before staging.

summary: P0150 (AIM) confirmed real, correctly classified, and non-duplicate via FERC Docket CP14-96-000 + independent press (WAMC, Utility Dive); staged REFS_ADDED for Capacity/Diameter/FuelSource/Location/SegmentCost/Start/Operator (Pressure UNRESOLVED, orphan ref flagged) plus 3 concerns -- an Owner-split attribution error (Enbridge's own factsheet gives AIM as 85% Enbridge/15% Eversource Energy, not the 100% Enbridge currently recorded), an EndState/Location scope concern (project actually continues into CT/RI/MA past the recorded Westchester County, NY endpoint), and a ProposalMonth spec error (FERC order says February 28, 2014, not August).
